new_this_week.title: Lucky — Ep 3
new_this_week.format: Limited series, 8 eps weekly Wed through 8/19
new_this_week.about: Ep 3 of Anya Taylor-Joy's Vegas-set heist thriller. Multi-million-dollar heist goes sideways; con artist Lucky is on the run from both the FBI and a ruthless crime boss. Based on Marissa Stapley's 2021 novel.
new_this_week.why: Two-ep premiere landed 7/15; Ep 3 is the tell for whether the ensemble (Bening, Olyphant, Ellis-Taylor) hooks you. Not top-priority genre, but Anya + novel adaptation + limited-series arc ticks three signals_what_lands.

new_this_week.title: The Dink
new_this_week.about: Washed-up former tennis prodigy Dusty Boyd (Jake Johnson) has been reduced to coaching unruly children at his father Chuck's (Ed Harris) suburban country club. Desperate for his father's approval, Dusty blindly supports Chuck's vendetta against the new craze taking over the club: pickleball. When he reaggravates an old injury, he resorts to the unthinkable — actually trying pickleball, with new partner Candace (Mary Steenburgen). Ben Stiller produces; cameos from Andy Roddick, John McEnroe, Patton Oswalt.
new_this_week.why: Ensemble comedy with a real bench — Jake Johnson + Mary Steenburgen + Ed Harris. Pickleball is left-field for you, but the fish-out-of-water beat is classic ensemble-comedy territory. Low-commitment single film, drops same day as Silo Ep 4.

new_this_week.title: 72 Hours
new_this_week.about: Kevin Hart plays a 40-year-old executive who accidentally gets invited to a Miami bachelor party with a group of Gen Zers. Directed by Tim Story (Ride Along, Barbershop, The Blackening); written by Matt Mider, Kevin Burrows, and Cobra Kai creators Jon Hurwitz & Hayden Schlossberg. Co-stars Marcello Hernández (SNL), Mason Gooding, Andy Garcia. R-rated.
new_this_week.why: Standard Kevin Hart odd-couple/fish-out-of-water setup. Cobra Kai writers give it slight upside; low-priority comedy but drops on the same big-content Friday as Silo Ep 4 and The Dink — worth a look if you want a lighter chaser.

new_this_week.title: Ransom Canyon — S2 (Complete, 8 eps)
new_this_week.about: Josh Duhamel and Minka Kelly return in Netflix's Western soap. Picks up six months after S1 — rancher Staten Kirkland fights to reclaim his legacy after being unseated as trustee of the Double K Ranch; musician Quinn O'Grady weighs small-town roots vs. New York City.
new_this_week.why: Skip — Western/family soap sits well outside your Sci-Fi/Fantasy/Comedy/Horror priorities and has no signals_what_lands overlap. Flagging so you don't wonder what the Thursday drop is.

new_this_week.title: The Hawk
new_this_week.about: Will Ferrell's first-ever TV comedy — a delusional washed-up golf legend Lonnie 'The Hawk' Hawkins chases one final major and drags everyone he loves into the chaos. Molly Shannon, Jimmy Tatro, Luke Wilson, Chris Parnell, Fortune Feimster support. PGA TOUR partnered.
new_this_week.why: Held from last week. 30-min ensemble comedy = bedtime slot. Ferrell/Shannon reunion + Chris Parnell = strong comic bench. Golf sub-genre is left-field, but it's really a workplace/family comedy in disguise.

new_this_week.title: Heartstopper Forever (Series Finale Film)
new_this_week.format: Feature film — the definitive series conclusion
new_this_week.about: The Heartstopper story ends as a 114-min film, replacing the planned S4. Nick heads to university; Charlie navigates a long-distance relationship in his final year. Alice Oseman writes and creates; Wash Westmore directs. Slightly grittier, more mature tone than the series.
new_this_week.why: Held from last week. LGBTQ+ inclusive + British + closure of a warm-hearted arc. Self-contained 1h54m film — no ongoing commitment.

new_this_week.title: Enola Holmes 3
new_this_week.about: Enola (Millie Bobby Brown) heads to Malta to marry Tewkesbury; Sherlock (Henry Cavill) disappears and she's pulled into a case. Directed by Philip Barantini (first non-Bradbeer entry).
new_this_week.why: 68% RT / 51% audience — considered the weakest of the trilogy, but a British mystery adventure with a strong lead if you want something breezy.

new_this_week.about: Bruce Timm / Matt Reeves / J.J. Abrams-produced noir-Batman animated series returns. S2 introduces Edward Nygma (Riddler), Carrie Kelley, Roxy Rocket, and — finally — The Joker. All 10 eps drop day-one 7/31.
